title: Dispenser
description: A dispenser for people living with restricted use of an upper limb. The project started with interviews about everyday routines, and a rose, thorn, bud synthesis that kept coming back to independence. The result is easy to use, with motion and voice activation, a plunger that dispenses liquids of any viscosity, and the option of a delivery service for refills.

brief.label: Objective
brief.text: Understand the everyday problems of people with a restricted upper limb, and find a solution for them.

brief.label: Design response
brief.text: A plunger dispenses liquids of any viscosity with ease, then retracts at the end of a reservoir's life so it can be swapped quickly.

brief.label: Compact storage
brief.text: Disassembly is as easy as pulling apart the o-rings that hold it together. For travel, users bring just the body and buy reservoirs locally, combining a whole host of soaps in one dispenser.

brief.label: Key features
brief.text: Motion sensor. Voice activation. Convenient refills, with an optional delivery service.

brief.label: Materials
brief.text: PLA (polylactic acid) for the dispenser: derived from renewable resources like sugar cane, biodegradable, low-shrinkage and insoluble in water, and best recycled at end of life. EPS (expanded polystyrene) for the packaging: cost-effective, recyclable, strong, and doesn't decay or harbor bacteria.

research_intro: Four interviews with people living with limited use of one arm mapped where the day gets hard. The morning routine came up again and again. A rose, thorn, bud synthesis then sorted what they valued, what hurt and what could grow, and pointed at independence as the need to design for. Names are withheld.

charts.title: Interviews
charts.caption: What each participant lives with, and where daily life gets hard.
charts.rows:
1|Loss of right lower-arm mobility|Operating a computer, sports, preparing food, carrying laundry, the morning routine (showering, brushing teeth)
2|Loss of left lower-arm mobility|Repeated breaks over time, severe pain, couldn't work, bathe for long periods or exercise; brushing teeth
3|No left-hand mobility|Opening doors and packages; the morning routine (brushing teeth, washing hair)
4|Loss of mobility in dominant arm|Getting changed, writing, seatbelts, relearning to brush teeth with the other hand, needing help with hair; the morning routine is exhausting

charts.title: Rose, thorn, bud
charts.caption: The last column is what stood out most in each row.
charts.rows:
Rose|New ways of doing things, a new community, closer to those who help, more attention|Constantly looked after
Thorn|Relearning with help, being labeled, less privacy, less time alone|Less independence
Bud|Expanded creativity, a new sense of purpose, building relationships, new chances to be recognized|Appreciates time alone

study_intro: Accessible design without looking like assistive equipment: soft, friendly forms that anyone would want in their bathroom.

study.label: Form
study.text: Rounded, egg-like modules that stack apart at o-rings, with nothing to grip or squeeze.

study.label: Interaction
study.text: Hands-free by default, with motion and voice, so the object asks nothing of the hand that's limited.

study.label: Color
study.text: Clean white bodies with bright blue packaging and accents: hygienic, calm and legible.

study.label: Packaging
study.text: A family of blue boxes, with a reservoir pack sized like a consumable, so refilling feels like restocking toothpaste, not servicing a device.
